chunks: And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Any believer whose believing brother asks him for his need while he is able to fulfill it, and he refuses him, Allah will impose on him a serpent in his grave that gnaws at his fingers.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of refusing to help a believer in need?
ai.summary: In the tradition of al-Ahwazi, this hadith emphasizes the spiritual weight of social responsibility, warning that a believer who neglects a capable peer faces a specific, visceral punishment: a serpent gnawing their fingers in the grave. This imagery underscores the connection between physical capability and moral obligation, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *ta'awun* (mutual assistance) as a core tenet of faith.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 119. It has been reported that Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) said:
If any believer asks his fellow brother to help him and he refuses while he is able to do, Allah will impose on him a serpent in his grave to bite his fingers.
